findings.claim: OME-Zarr 0.5 is implemented on Zarr format v3; all Zarr features (codecs, chunk grids, chunk key encodings, data types, storage transformers) may be used unless explicitly disallowed; no explicit disallowances appear in the capture.

An image is a Zarr group with 'multiscales' (and optionally 'omero') in zarr.json attributes; each level is a separate array; level array names are arbitrary, ordering defined by multiscales metadata.
Image arrays up to 5-dimensional; axis order time before channel before spatial; dimensionality variable 2-5; axis names arbitrary.
OME-Zarr metadata stored under namespaced key 'ome' in attributes with string version; version MUST be consistent within a hierarchy.
Three image-discovery layouts: plain sibling image groups; bioformats2raw collections (transitional) with optional OME/series; HCS plate/well trees with mandatory well/plate specifications.
bioformats2raw.layout value MUST be '3'; if present with plate, plate takes precedence; image collections and plates cannot be mixed at present; plate images MUST be at defined locations.
OME group MAY contain 'series'; when present it MUST be a list of string paths whose order MUST match OME-XML Image order if provided.
b2raw collections SHOULD have OME/METADATA.ome.xml; it MUST adhere to OME-XML and MUST use MetadataOnly (no BinData/BinaryOnly/TiffData); MAY use minimum spec.
Readers SHOULD surface multiple images (SHOULD NOT default to first); MAY use series; MAY show all or offer choice; MAY ignore other groups/arrays under root.
Without series and without plate, multiscales images MUST be in consecutively numbered groups starting at 0, each representing exactly one OME-XML Image in order.
HCS: three groups above images; well group MUST implement well spec; plate group MUST implement plate spec; empty rows/wells SHOULD NOT be present.

Plate dictionary MUSTs: columns, rows, wells, version (string); SHOULD: field_count, name; MAY: acquisitions; column/row names alphanumeric, case-sensitive, unique; well path MUST be <row>/<column>, no extra dirs; rowIndex/columnIndex 0-based and consistent with path.

Well dictionary MUST contain images; each MUST have path (alphanumeric, case-sensitive, unique); acquisition key MUST when plate has multiple acquisitions; well version SHOULD with MUST-string-when-present.
axes: name MUST (unique); type SHOULD (space/time/channel, custom MAY); unit SHOULD (UDUNITS-2 strings enumerated L171-L172); axes length MUST equal array dimensionality.
dimension_names MUST be included in array zarr.json of a multiscale level and MUST match axes names (MUST clarified in 0.5.2).

multiscales: list of dicts; axes MUST 2-5 entries equal to array dims; 2-3 space axes; MAY one time, MAY one channel/null/custom; order MUST be time, channel/custom, space; zyx SHOULD for anisotropic z.
datasets MUST list levels with relative paths ordered largest (highest resolution) to smallest; same dimension count <=5 corresponding to axes.

Each dataset MUST have exactly one scale transformation (physical size or time duration); unavailable scaling MUST use inter-level factor defaulting 1.0; MAY one translation after scale; vector lengths MUST equal axes; only scale/translation allowed at this position.
multiscales-level coordinateTransformations MAY exist, apply to all levels, follow same type/order rules, and are applied after per-dataset transforms.

Transform types: identity (default, typically implicit), translation, scale; vectors may be inline float lists or binary data at a 'path' in the container; applied sequentially in order. Binary path variant lacks layout detail in capture (unresolved U3).
multiscales is a list (multiple pyramids possible); selection guidance (use single; else user chooses by name; fallback first) appears only in example/pseudocode form, non-normative per L877-L883.
omero (transitional) is optional; if present MUST contain channels; each channel MUST have color (6 hex digits) and window with MUST fields min, max, start, end.

omero example shows id, name, per-channel active/coefficient/family/inverted/label and rdefs defaultT/defaultZ/model; these appear only in the annotated example (non-normative); OMERO WebGateway docs referenced but not in capture.
labels group nested in image group; labels-group zarr.json MUST contain 'labels' key listing paths to label images; all label images SHOULD be listed; intermediate groups MUST NOT contain metadata.
Label image pixels MUST be integer types: uint8/int8/uint16/int16/uint32/int32/uint64/int64.
Label image zarr.json MUST implement multiscales; datasets MUST have same number of scale levels as the original unlabeled image.
image-label SHOULD exist with colors (MUST be array) and version (MUST be string); readers SHOULD display using colors; each entry MUST have integer label-value; rgba MAY (4 ints 0-255, 4th alpha).
image-label MAY contain properties (entries MUST have label-value; arbitrary kv; keys may differ across entries) and source (MUST be object; MAY include image relative path; default '../../').
JSON comments MUST NOT be included in JSON objects (spec example comments are for clarity only).
Transitional metadata: implementations may be expected (MUST) or encouraged (SHOULD) to support reading; writing usually MAY.
Released version is 0.5; editor's-draft data not necessarily supported; 0.5.2 added dimension_names MUST; 0.5.0 introduced Zarr v3.
Hierarchy may equally live on HTTP/object storage; format is storage-neutral; local-only reading is a product boundary, not a format property.
Multi-word keys should be camelCase but legacy exceptions exist (e.g. bioformats2raw.layout, field_count, image-label, label-value as used in document); parsers must not normalize key casing.
Labels under an HCS field of view are optional.
Each label dimension should equal the corresponding image dimension or be 1 if irrelevant; observed in layout annotations, not as an RFC-2119 sentence.
Plate 'version' is MUST per normative text but both plate examples omit the key; real files may lack it.
Conformance boilerplate claims RFC2119 words do not appear in all uppercase, contradicting pervasive uppercase usage; adopted reading: uppercase keywords are normative (L872-L874, L57-L59).
Index lists 'HCS, in § 2.2.3' while HCS hierarchy is §1.2.
Stray '.' line in HCS hierarchy diagram.
Implementations section contains only 'See Tools.' — no implementation/tool evidence exists in the admitted capture; brief's reader-implementation dimension cannot be evidenced in scope.
rdefs semantics and the channels-array-matches-c-dimension rule appear only in annotated examples, non-normative per L877-L883.
Multiscale-selection pseudocode/fallback is example material; normative status of the fallback rule is not established.
Mixed requirement constructions ('SHOULD contain a key whose value MUST be ...') separate presence level from value level; readers must not conflate.
Spec's own JSON examples include comments despite the comments ban for objects (L65-L66); strict parsing of real files still required.
